criteria.criterion: CHANGELOG.md and the new decisions.md entry name the root cause: the decision log is prose with no link from a decision to the code or limit it governs, so reversals were found only at the final verdict.
criteria.evidence: I read the diff. The CHANGELOG Unreleased entry and the new D156 entry in docs/decisions.md both contain: "The decision log is prose with no link from a decision to the code or limit it governs, so reversals were found only at the final verdict." Both also name the two jobs. The test decisions::tests::the_root_cause_is_named_in_the_changelog_and_the_log passed. It runs in the athena-cli lib target, not `--bin athena` as the plan said. I used the release profile because a stale debug artifact in the shared target directory broke the debug build (see findings).

criteria.criterion: docs/decision-links.toml holds a `[[governs]]` list with at least D08 mapped to the snapshot/history code paths, and ConfirmedLinks parsing in crates/athena-cli/src/decisions.rs reads and validates it (unknown decision ids are an error).
criteria.evidence: In docs/decision-links.toml, a `[[governs]]` entry maps D08 to crates/athena-git/src/snapshot.rs and crates/athena-core/src/run/candidate.rs. This matches D08's text (snapshot building and the candidate commit). ConfirmedLinks gains a `governs` field. `parse` calls athena_data::decision_links::parse_governs, which rejects a malformed id, empty paths, an absolute or `..` path, and unknown fields. `unknown_governed` plus backtest `check_governs` make an id missing from the log a condition (a) finding. Strictly, that check is a backtest finding, not a parse error. Tests that passed: a_malformed_governs_entry_is_an_error, an_unknown_governed_decision_is_reported, the_real_list_maps_d08_..., and the backtest condition-(a) test.

findings.summary: The producer is not told in advance which paths are governed, so its first attempt at any governed path fails the whole job, and the finding only arrives through a manual retry.
findings.evidence: No producer brief mentions docs/decision-links.toml or governed paths (grep over crates/ finds the term only in decision_links.rs, checks.rs, reading.rs, the tests and the CLI). D156 lists in-loop send-back as follow-up (d). Simpler or more correct alternative: list the decisions that govern the files the producer may touch in its brief, or send the gate back inside the producer loop the way the replay is. producer.rs and briefs.rs are out of scope for this job, so this is a named follow-up, not a defect.

findings.summary: A change to a governed file that reverses nothing still needs a new entry in the append-only decision log, which will fill the log with 'checked and stands' entries.
findings.evidence: decision_links::unreconciled accepts only a new `[[link]]` whose `newer` is a new heading. By the producer's own count (an estimate I did not re-measure), 8 of the last 200 commits touched the two D08 files. A lighter acknowledgement would avoid the clutter, for example a `checked` record in the toml or a commit trailer naming the decision.

summary: The change passes. It fixes the root cause the request named, that nothing linked a decision to the code it governs. docs/decision-links.toml gets a validated `[[governs]]` list, with D08 mapped to the snapshot and candidate code. One shared rule in athena_data::decision_links runs at the top of check_and_verify, before CI, the pull request, the checks and the verifier. A change to a governed path then fails the job with the decision ids, unless it adds a new log entry with a matching link. The retry brief carries those ids to the next producer. The drain help ceiling is now built from MAX_CONCURRENCY_CEILING. I ran the tests that show the behavior: 15 pure-rule tests over D08, D12 and D02; end-to-end jobs where an unreconciled edit fails before the verifier (verifier count 0) while a reconciled edit and an ungoverned edit reach it; the retry-brief and retry_findings tests; the drain-help tests; the decisions and backtest tests; and the refusal corpus. All passed. For the athena-cli tests I used the release profile because the debug build hit a stale artifact in the shared target directory. Athena's recorded fmt, clippy and test runs passed. I found no blocker or major problem. Four minor findings remain: the producer is not told in advance which paths are governed, so the first attempt fails and needs a retry; a change that reverses nothing still adds a decision-log entry; only D08 and the drain ceiling are covered so far; and four planned files sit outside the deliverables list.
